type_and_flow_constraints: $ITERABLE and $LIST are finite (arrays, Collections, Maps or bounded index ranges)
$KEY_invariant and any other inputs to $PRED/$PRED2 are loop-invariant with respect to the iterated loop(s)
$found is monotonic (only false -> true inside the loop); it is not reset to false in the loop
$remaining is a small bounded counter (e.g., K in {1..N_small}); decremented only when goals are met; loop outcome does not require processing beyond fulfilling all goals
$res is either (a) a single-result variable overwritten on matches and consumed after the loop, or (b) unused inside the loop except for the overwrite
For Map scans: if $PRED compares entry.getKey() to $KEY_invariant, assume key uniqueness (or intent of uniqueness) so additional iterations are unnecessary after the first hit
$OPTIONAL_SINK/$SIDE_EFFECTS_ENABLED are invariant in the loop; when false/null, no required per-iteration effects remain once goals are met
For the last-match variant: $LIST is an ordered List; selecting the last matching element is the intent; correctness is preserved by reverse iteration with early break
For the nested form: inner-loop flag ($any) feeds an outer-loop fold ($all via && or OR-equivalent); once $any==true or $all==false/true (absorbing), further iterations are semantically redundant
matching_rules: Find For/EnhancedFor/While loop(s) that implement a search-like pattern: an if-branch with predicate $PRED over the current element and loop-invariant key/target

Inside the match branch, detect one or more of: (a) assignment to an outer-scoped result variable $res; (b) monotonic boolean update $found = true or $found |= <cond>; (c) decrement of a small counter $remaining-- indicating bounded goals; (d) an expensive/terminal action whose repetition is unnecessary
The variables updated in the match branch ($res/$found/$remaining) are used only after the loop (or folded after the inner loop) to steer control or produce the final result
No control-flow transfer (no break/return/throw) is present on the same path immediately after the first successful match or after all goals are satisfied
Boolean OR/ANY pattern: inside the loop, $flag = $flag || <cond> or if (<cond>) $flag = true;, and $flag is tested only after the loop
Boolean AND/ALL dual: $flag starts true and is updated as $flag = $flag && <cond> or if (!<cond>) $flag = false;, and is consumed after the loop without early exit on the absorbing value
Multi-goal pattern: multiple flags (or a counter) indicate pending goals; each goal is set/cleared at most once; no exit when all goals are achieved
Nested loops: inner loop sets $any (existence flag) without break; outer loop combines into $all via logical AND/OR without early exit on the absorbing result
Map-lookup pattern: iterating map.entrySet/keySet/values while comparing to $KEY_invariant and assigning/using a single result, without break/return

Sequential gated scans: two consecutive loops guarded by the same invariant gate with opposite polarity (if ($FLAG) ... in loop B, if (!$FLAG) ... in loop A); only one branch is semantically relevant per call, yet both loops execute without hoisting the gate
negative_constraints: Do not match loops that intentionally aggregate across all elements (e.g., sum, count, collect into list/map, compute min/max without an early-termination condition)
Do not match if later iterations must run for required side effects (I/O, logging, metrics) that are mandated regardless of matches and regardless of $OPTIONAL_SINK/$SIDE_EFFECTS_ENABLED
Do not match if the observed behavior depends on processing all matches (e.g., deliberate last-wins semantics over an unordered container, or correctness depends on evaluating all candidates)

Do not match when the loop already short-circuits on all feasible paths after meeting the goal(s) (presence of break/return/throw in the match branch or loop condition uses the flag, e.g., while(!$found) ...)
Do not match if boolean flags are non-monotonic (e.g., $found toggles true->false) or $res is refined by considering all elements (e.g., best-of reduction requiring full scan)
Do not match last-match optimization if the container is unordered (Set, Hash-based without order guarantees) or reverse traversal is not semantically equivalent
signals: Assignment to a boolean like found/any/exists/matched inside a loop without a subsequent break/return
Pattern: flag = flag || <cond>(elem) or if (<cond>(elem)) flag = true; with post-loop usage of flag
Pattern: result = ... inside if (predicate(elem, TARGET)); result read after the loop; no early exit
Comparisons like equals(TARGET), compareTo(...) == 0, startsWith/endsWith/contains inside loops
Loop over Map.entrySet()/keySet()/values() used to locate a specific key/value; suggest map.get(TARGET) or containsKey
Multiple small goal flags or a remaining counter updated in-loop without a break when all goals satisfied
Nested search: if (!any) any = predicate(...); then outer result = result && any; without breaks
Optional sink guard present (if (sink != null) {...}) where sink-disabled path still continues scanning after match
Static analysis hints: 'Loop can be terminated early', 'Search loop without break/return', 'Replace loop with map.get/contains'

do-while or while loop over a queue/worklist (e.g., Deque, Queue) that checks a condition like typeA.asErasure().equals(typeB) or typeA.isAssignableTo(typeB) but never breaks or returns early once the match is found — all elements always processed
Nested for-loops iterating two collections where typeA.equals(typeB) or leftType.equals(rightType) is checked in the body but no early break/return is present on a confirmed match

type_and_flow_constraints: E⟨R, A*⟩ is a value-producing expression evaluated multiple times within one control step; categories include: method call R.m(A*), field read R.f (possibly volatile/shared), array access ARR[IDX], and container bound BOUND⟨C⟩ ∈ {C.length, C.length(), C.size()}

Purity/determinism: for method calls, E has no side effects and its result depends only on its inputs (receiver R and arguments A*), or it is an external/state query whose freshness is not required within the same control step
Invariance: R, A*, C, ARR, and IDX are not mutated (nor via aliases) between the repeated evaluations; for loop bounds, BOUND⟨C⟩ is loop-invariant over the iteration

Concurrency: if reading a shared/volatile field F, snapshot F into a local once per control step to ensure a consistent view and to reduce volatile read cost; do not rely on multiple rereads for visibility within the same step
Short-circuit awareness: if E is hoisted out of a boolean short-circuit, guard hoisting behind existing cheap preconditions so E is still only evaluated on paths where it would have been evaluated
Polling loops: when the surrounding construct intentionally waits/sleeps, compute E once per iteration and refresh only after a wait/signal or explicit state-change point
matching_rules: Within a single basic block, boolean expression, or one loop iteration, find two or more syntactically equivalent subexpressions S1 ≡ S2 ≡ E⟨R, A*⟩ with identical receiver and arguments
Categories to match: (a) MethodInvocation R.m(A*); (b) FieldAccess or QualifiedName R.f; (c) ArrayAccess ARR[IDX]; (d) BOUND⟨C⟩ in a loop header or body
Verify that none of {R, A*, C, ARR, IDX} is assigned to, mutated, or may be mutated via an alias on any path between S1 and S2 within the control step
For loop bounds: detect ForStatement/WhileStatement where the condition contains BOUND⟨C⟩ and the loop body does not change C (no adds/removes/appends/reassignments affecting the bound)
For polling/wait loops: detect repeated E⟨R, A*⟩ in a single condition or iteration together with WAIT/SLEEP/TIMEOUT usage; suggest caching once per iteration and refreshing after the wait/event
For shared/volatile fields: detect multiple reads of the same field identifier within a single expression/branch (e.g., ternary or chained condition); suggest snapshot to a local variable
negative_constraints: Exclude expressions with side effects or non-idempotent behavior: iterator.next(), stream.read(), random/time sources, counters that advance state, I/O that must be reissued
Exclude cases where any operand (receiver R, arguments A*, container C, array ARR, index IDX) may be mutated between occurrences or via an intervening call with side effects on those operands
Exclude polling/spin loops that intentionally reread a volatile/atomic field to observe changes without a wait/sleep boundary

Exclude hoisting that would increase work due to short-circuiting on the common path (e.g., a cheap precondition prevents evaluating E most of the time and E would become eagerly evaluated); only hoist after guarding with the same preconditions
Exclude array/field reads that are volatile or concurrently modified when a single-snapshot semantic would be incorrect for the intended behavior within the step

For external API calls in tight polling loops, exclude obviously cheap O(1) pure accessors on in-memory collections unless they occur in loop bounds (where per-iteration re-evaluation still adds overhead)
signals: Multiple identical MethodInvocation tokens in one If/While condition: e.g., foo.count(x) >= t || foo.count(x) > 0
Repeated occurrences of arr[idx] in the same statement or small block
Loop conditions like i < list.size() or i < sb.length() where the receiver is not modified in the loop body
Single return or ternary using the same field name multiple times: return F == null ? ... : (F instanceof T ? (T) F : ...)
Presence of WAIT/SLEEP/timeouts with repeated state-query calls in the same condition/iteration
Utilities and pure APIs repeatedly invoked with identical arguments (e.g., Character.getType(c), Math.* on invariant operands)

collection.size() used as the bound of a for-loop (i < collection.size()) AND called again inside the same loop body (e.g., Math.min(collection.size(), x) or array allocation new T[collection.size()]) with no mutation of the collection between calls — two or more redundant size() evaluations

Same method like .indexOf(char), .getAnnotationType(), .getParameterTypes(), .getParameters(), .size() invoked more than once on the same receiver within the same method without caching the result in a local variable

type_and_flow_constraints: computeR, new V(...), and new H(...) are expensive (e.g., parsing, resource loading, complex graph build, heavy math) and pure w.r.t. the stable inputs used for caching; H must expose init/reset or equivalent to safely reuse.
Inputs captured in @stableState/@invariantCfg/args_subset are stable across typical call sequences or can be normalized into a stable Key; no hidden time/random/external mutable dependencies.
R/V are immutable, read-only, or otherwise safe to reuse for the same key; H is not thread-safe unless confined via ThreadLocal or equivalent.
If a backing store (e.g., dictionary/map/field) influences the cached value, all mutations to that store flow through methods that also update or invalidate the cache (coherence).

KeyK must define value-based equals/hashCode across all semantics-affecting fields; arrays or collections use Arrays.equals/hashCode or element-wise hashing; consider defensive copies/normalization to ensure stability.

@SENTINEL is a value distinguishable from valid results (null, UNSET constant, NaN-sentinel, etc.); minor benign races in first computation are acceptable only if the computation is pure and idempotent.
If calls cross threads, use ConcurrentMap/volatile/synchronization or ThreadLocal caches; avoid sharing mutable H across threads.
matching_rules: Find a frequently invoked method M (getter/accessor/processing hot path) that, on each call, constructs an object via `new T(...)` or performs an expensive computation whose inputs are dominated by class fields, constant keys, or otherwise loop-invariant expressions.
No pre-existing memoized field or cache lookup guards the expensive path; the constructed object is immediately returned or used and discarded.

Parameterless or constant-argument getters: detect `new R(backing.get(CONST_KEY))` or equivalent transformations inside a no-arg method; optional paired setter writes the same backing entry without cache maintenance.

Helper allocation per call: detect construction of helper H (or via F.resolve(...)) with mostly invariant constructor args, immediate use, and disposal; H exposes init/reset but was not reused prior to the fix.

Keyed construction on hot paths: detect repeated `new V(ctx, p1..pk)` where (ctx, p1..pk) are stable or repeat frequently; no factory/caching present; after fix, calls route through a factory/cache using a Key with equals/hashCode.

Cache ineffectiveness due to identity keys: detect a type used as a key in hash-based collections without overriding equals/hashCode (identity semantics); fix introduces value-based equals/hashCode enabling dedup/cache hits.

Subclass bypassing base cache: base class has a private cached-helper method; a subclass directly does `new RES(...)` for the same resource; fix widens visibility (protected final) or exposes accessors so subclass reuses the cache.
negative_constraints: Exclude cases where fresh instances are required per call (e.g., defensive copies, unique mutable objects, timestamps, random, or side-effecting constructors).
Exclude computations depending on frequently changing external state not invalidated by this class (e.g., external map mutated elsewhere) unless an explicit invalidation strategy exists.
Exclude objects whose constructors have observable side effects that must occur on every call (I/O effects, counters, metrics) or whose reuse is semantically incorrect.
Exclude scenarios where parameters vary with high entropy per call, making cache hit rates negligible or incorrect.

Exclude cases lacking safe equality semantics for keys (non-deterministic floats, missing stable normalization) or where arrays/collections remain mutable without copy/immutability, breaking key stability.
Exclude trivial/cheap operations (simple field reads, primitive boxing) where caching does not materially improve performance.
Exclude multi-threaded access to non-thread-safe caches or helpers without confinement or proper synchronization.
signals: Introduction of fields like `private R cached;` with null/sentinel checks; patterns: `if (cached == null) cached = compute...(); return cached;`
Addition of Map-based caches: WeakHashMap/ConcurrentMap, computeIfAbsent, factory classes routing creation through `create(...)`.
ThreadLocal caches/helpers and calls to `init(...)`, `reset(...)`, `configure(...)` on reused helpers.
Setters updated to also assign/invalidate a cache field; numeric caches using sentinel constants (e.g., Float.NEGATIVE_INFINITY).
Refactoring from direct `new V(...)` in hot paths to `factory.create(...)`; addition of a Key class with equals/hashCode (Arrays.equals/hashCode for arrays).
Commit messages or comments mentioning cache/memoize/reuse/performance, or warnings/profiling pointing to allocations in getters or helper constructors.
Dictionary/backing lookups with constant keys (e.g., getDictionaryObject(CONST_KEY)) formerly repeated per call and now cached.

Accessor method get(int index) that returns new ConcreteWrapper(underlyingArray[index]) or new Impl(field, list.get(index), visitor) on every call with no cache or lazy-init field — fresh allocation per access

Method body calls resolver.resolve(x), baseNameResolver.resolve(x), getCanonicalName(), or getName() on a field/parameter on every invocation with no instance field caching the result; method has no parameters that differ between calls

root_cause: Redundant per-call encoding/formatting due to inefficient API usage
type_and_flow_constraints: SINK_B is an OutputStream or any sink that accepts byte[].
SINK_C is a Writer, StringBuilder, StringBuffer, or Appendable; when appending hex or text, it accepts char sequences.
CS (or CS_NAME) is loop- and call-invariant within the emitting method; it does not change across the optimized calls.
STR_LITi are string literals or compile-time constants that are written multiple times; safe to pre-encode once.
When replacing String.format in loops, FMT_HEX is a fixed-width numeric format (e.g., %02X or %04X) and VALUE_EXTRACTOR yields an integral value per element.
DEC (CharsetDecoder) must be per-instance or ThreadLocal (not shared across threads) due to non-thread-safety.
The optimized overload selection (Charset vs name) must be semantically equivalent for the chosen charset.
For CharSequence specialization, X is known at call sites to be CharSequence (or subtype) frequently; concatenation can legally use StringBuilder.append(CharSequence).
Avoiding bytes->String->bytes round-trips is only valid if the downstream sink ultimately needs bytes in the same charset.
matching_rules: Detect call sites inside hot methods or loops that perform String.getBytes(CONST_CHARSET_OR_NAME) on string literals or fixed tokens more than once.
Detect helper methods that accept String and immediately call getBytes(CONST_CHARSET_OR_NAME) to write to an OutputStream.
Detect new String(byte[], [off, len], CONST_CHARSET_OR_NAME) immediately followed by getBytes of the same charset or writing via String to a byte sink (round-trip).
Detect String.format with fixed-width hex patterns (%02X, %04X, etc.) invoked per element inside loops, or helper methods used in loops that contain such String.format calls.
Detect per-byte hex built via Integer.toHexString(...).substring(...).toUpperCase(), or helpers returning per-byte String/byte[] used in loops.
Detect repeated new String(byte[], off, len, CONST_CHARSET_OR_NAME) in hot paths without a cached CharsetDecoder.
Detect concatenation or utility methods combining String + Object (or generic toString) where frequent call sites pass CharSequence; no (String, CharSequence) overload exists.
Detect conversions using Charset overloads (or name overloads) in hot utilities without any environment-dependent strategy selecting the fastest equivalent overload.
negative_constraints: Do not match if strings are highly dynamic per call and not safe or beneficial to pre-encode.
Do not match when the sink is character-only (Writer) and the code correctly works with chars rather than bytes; direct byte writing would change behavior.
Do not match if the charset varies per call or is data-dependent; caching or pre-encoding could change semantics.
Do not match loops that already use lookup tables and preallocated buffers for hex encoding without per-iteration String or array allocation.
Do not match cold paths (initialization, error handling) where the overhead is irrelevant.
Do not match if a reusable CharsetDecoder/encoder is already maintained per instance or via ThreadLocal.
Do not match if specialized formatting semantics (locale, case mapping, custom rules) require String.format or Integer.toHexString(+ transforms).
Do not match if overload selection is constrained by semantics (e.g., custom Charset subclass) or an existing strategy already adapts by runtime.
signals: Frequent .getBytes("UTF-8"|"ISO-8859-1"|CONST) on string literals in hot code.
append*(String) methods that immediately convert to bytes for OutputStream writes.
new String(byte[], [off, len], CS) followed by getBytes(CS) or writing to an OutputStream.
String.format("%02X"|"%04X", ...) inside loops or toHex helpers used in loops.
Integer.toHexString(...).substring(...).toUpperCase() inside byte-processing loops.
Helpers named toHex/stringToHex/byteToHexString/byteToHexBytes returning small objects per byte.
Multiple new String(byte[], ...) calls in parsing/deserialization loops; nearby Charset.forName calls.
Concatenation patterns like s + String.valueOf(x) or framework toString(x) where x is often CharSequence; missing (String, CharSequence) overload.
Static final Charset fields (e.g., UTF_8) used across conversions without runtime adaptation logic.

root_cause: Inefficient data structures and bad API usage (boxed numbers/containers on hot numeric paths)
type_and_flow_constraints: BOXED_T ∈ {java.lang.Integer, java.lang.Long, java.lang.Float, java.lang.Double, java.lang.Boolean}
PRIM_T = unbox(BOXED_T) ∈ {int, long, float, double, boolean}
WRAPPER_NUM ∈ {Integer, Long, Float, Double, Number, Boolean} or library-specific numeric wrappers (e.g., COSNumber, COSFloat)
CONTAINER is an object-based numeric container (e.g., List<Number>, custom Array<Number>, library numeric array) whose elements are WRAPPER_NUM
Field f is never assigned null and is not used in contexts requiring a reference (no identity checks, no synchronization on f, no storing f as Object)
NUMERIC_USE consists of arithmetic/boolean operations or passing as parameters that accept primitives/autounbox
In compute path, either: (a) a conversion method exists (TO_PRIM_ARRAY, FROM_PRIM_ARRAY), or (b) the container exposes element getters returning WRAPPER_NUM and setters/adders accepting WRAPPER_NUM
Boxing/unboxing is observed along hot paths: NEW WRAPPER_NUM(PRIM) or valueOf(PRIM), and WRAPPER_NUM.[int|long|float|double|boolean]Value()
No container-specific semantics (beyond sequential numeric storage) are needed for the computation (no sparse behavior, aliasing-sensitive views, or mutation-order reliance)
matching_rules: Field pattern: find a field declaration of type BOXED_T; dataflow shows no null assignments, no comparisons with null, no synchronization/identity/equality on reference; all uses of the field are compatible with primitives or autounboxing

Loop/container pattern: inside a loop, detect writes of PRIM to a numeric container via set/add resulting in implicit boxing, and reads from the container followed by immediate unboxing via .<prim>Value()

Method pattern: a method that accepts and/or returns CONTAINER<WRAPPER_NUM> converts to PRIM[] (via TO_PRIM_ARRAY or manual unboxing loop), performs numeric computation on PRIM, then reconstructs the container by per-element boxing/add

Presence of an alternative primitive path is suggested by any of: methods like toFloatArray()/toDoubleArray()/setPrimitiveArray(...), overloads accepting PRIM[]/returning PRIM[], or utility conversion helpers
Confirm that replacing BOXED_T with PRIM_T and CONTAINER<WRAPPER_NUM> with PRIM[] preserves behavior for non-null numeric values along the hot path
negative_constraints: Do not match if nullability of the field/element is semantically required (optional/tri-state, union-with-null schema, explicit null assignments or checks)

Do not match if APIs require the boxed type or Object reference identity (e.g., the field/container elements are used as keys where null is meaningful, or passed to reflection/collections expecting Object of the boxed type)
Do not match if code synchronizes on the boxed object, relies on reference equality, or uses weak/identity maps with boxed instances
Do not match for BigDecimal/BigInteger or other numerical classes where primitive substitution changes semantics/precision
Do not match if the container provides primitive getters/setters already used (no boxing/unboxing in the hot path)
Do not match if the transform is invoked outside the loop with results reused across iterations without per-iteration boxing/unboxing
signals: Field declarations: '(public|protected|private) (Integer|Long|Float|Double|Boolean) [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*;'
Hot-loop unboxing calls: '.floatValue()', '.doubleValue()', '.intValue()', '.longValue()', '.booleanValue()'
Per-iteration allocations: 'new Integer(', 'Integer.valueOf(', 'new Float(', 'Float.valueOf(' inside loops
Container mutations in loops: 'container.add(new ...)', 'container.set(i, new ...)'
Conversions around compute: 'toFloatArray()', 'toDoubleArray()', 'toPrimitiveArray()', 'setFloatArray(...)', 'setPrimitiveArray(...)'
Imports/usages of Number-like wrappers in performance-critical code (e.g., COSNumber/COSFloat in PDF processing)
Compiler warnings: -Xlint:boxing/-Xlint:unboxing near hot code

root_cause: Inefficient or bad API usage (per-element accessors instead of bulk row/array operations)
type_and_flow_constraints: SRC, DST ∈ {java.awt.image.BufferedImage, java.awt.image.Raster/WritableRaster} or wrappers providing per-element and bulk accessors
API_GET_ELEM ∈ {Raster.getPixel, Raster.getSample, BufferedImage.getRGB(x,y), WritableRaster.getPixel, ColorModel.getDataElement(...) per pixel, custom per-element read}
API_SET_ELEM ∈ {WritableRaster.setPixel, WritableRaster.setSample, BufferedImage.setRGB(x,y), Raster.setDataElements per pixel, custom per-element write}
API_GET_BULK ∈ {Raster.getPixels, Raster.getSamples, Raster.getDataElements(rect,...), BufferedImage.getRGB(x,y,w,h,int[],off,scan), stream.read(byte[],off,len), NIO bulk get}

API_SET_BULK ∈ {WritableRaster.setPixels, WritableRaster.setSamples, WritableRaster.setDataElements(rect,...), BufferedImage.setRGB(x,y,w,h,int[],off,scan), setData/copyData, Graphics.drawImage with whole-rect}
API_COPY_OR_SET_DATA ∈ {BufferedImage.setData(Raster), Raster.copyData(WritableRaster), WritableRaster.setRect, ComponentSampleModel/DataBuffer bank sharing}
ELEM is a pixel/sample scalar or small tuple (e.g., int, byte, int[CHANNELS], byte[CHANNELS]); ARR is a primitive array holding a contiguous row/rect of elements
ELEM_STRIDE = number of primitive entries per element in ARR (e.g., CHANNELS for interleaved/banded layouts)
PURE_TRANSFORM_PER_ELEM/IN_PLACE has no dependency on neighbors or non-contiguous positions; no loop-carried state except within the element
HEIGHT_EXPR, WIDTH_EXPR are loop-invariant; they may be cached or called once per row
For the optional byte-aligned fast path: BPC == 8, DECODE_IS_DEFAULT matches the color space default, COLOR_KEY_IS_NULL, and SRC_RASTER.getDataBuffer() is DataBufferByte
If constructing ColorModel/BufferedImage from a Raster, the ColorModel's data type matches SRC_RASTER.getDataBuffer().getDataType() to avoid implicit repacking
Buffers (REUSABLE_BUF/ROW) are reused across iterations to avoid per-iteration allocations
matching_rules: Find a loop over two indices (X,Y) or equivalent nested iteration covering image/grid bounds; inner body invokes per-element accessor pairs (API_GET_ELEM and/or API_SET_ELEM)
OR find full-image per-pixel copy using SRC.getRGB(x,y) -> DST.setRGB(x,y, ...) with no intermediate transformation
OR find a generic per-sample decoding path that performs bit-unpacking and per-sample loops even when bpc == 8 and decode equals the color space default
Transformation inside the inner loop uses only the current element/pixel's components; no references to neighboring coordinates (X±1,Y±1, etc.)
Width/height (or bounds) are loop-invariant; may be obtained via method calls inside or outside the loop
Optional: detect ColorModel created with hard-coded DataBuffer.TYPE_XXX while pairing with a Raster variable, suggesting potential repacking overhead that blocks bulk paths
negative_constraints: Do not match if any step already uses bulk row/rect APIs (getPixels/setPixels, getDataElements/setDataElements with arrays, getRGB/setRGB with arrays, copyData/setData) inside the loop body
Do not match algorithms that depend on neighbor pixels, convolution windows, or non-linear access patterns that prevent contiguous block processing
Exclude sparse updates (e.g., conditional writes to a minority of pixels) where bulk operations would move unnecessary data

Exclude cases requiring filters/predictors or decoding steps that mandate per-sample processing (e.g., non-byte-aligned bpc, non-default decode, color key/mask present) unless an equivalent bulk path is proven
Exclude when destination/source types are provably fixed and already optimal (e.g., DataBuffer.TYPE_BYTE with existing banked/bulk code), or when memory layout forbids safe bulk copy
signals: Grep: .getPixel(, .setPixel(, .getSample(, .setSample( inside nested for-loops over x and y
Grep: getRGB(x,y) and setRGB(x,y,...) used inside loops covering full width*height
Presence of temporary int[]/byte[] arrays used only to pass to per-pixel get/set calls
High profiler hot spots in Raster/BufferedImage per-pixel methods or ImageInputStream.readBits during 8-bit image processing
Instantiation of ColorModel with literal DataBuffer.TYPE_XXX while a Raster is in scope for pairing
Absence of getPixels/setPixels, getDataElements/setDataElements, setData/copyData, or bulk getRGB/setRGB overloads

root_cause: Inefficient or bad API usage, Inefficient algorithms
type_and_flow_constraints: $src ∈ {java.io.InputStream, java.net.URL, java.io.File, javax.imageio.stream.ImageInputStream}
$reader : javax.imageio.ImageReader; $params may be null or ImageReadParam
$img,$outImg : java.awt.image.BufferedImage
$wr : java.awt.image.WritableRaster; its sample model/component count is compatible with $cs when a direct wrap is viable
$cs,$genericCS : java.awt.color.ColorSpace (incl. ICC_ColorSpace)
$IN,$OUT : java.awt.image.Raster/WritableRaster or raw arrays accessed via getPixel/getDataElements/setPixel/setDataElements
$H,$W,$N are derived from the source dimensions and cover the full image/array (inner loop hot path)
In shape B, $CONVERTER.$toRGBImageMethod returns a new BufferedImage and copies/converts pixels internally
In shape C, at least one of: java.lang.Math.pow used per component; ColorSpace.getInstance(...)/toRGB called per sample; repeated matrix.getValue(i,j) in the loop; per-iteration array allocations
In shape D, out is created from in (createCompatible* or same shape) and a full copy (setRect/arraycopy of full length) occurs before a traversal that overwrites most/all elements

$STATE.indicatesInvisibleOrModeRequiresInversion() denotes zero-opacity/INVISIBLE rendering mode or a mask mode that requires different alpha semantics (soft vs explicit); $OPAQUE_COLOR is a java.awt.Color without alpha (alpha=255)
matching_rules: Match if ANY of the following subpatterns is present:

A) Convenience decode misuse: a call to javax.imageio.ImageIO.read($src) occurs on a path where the image format is known or complex (e.g., JBIG2, JPEG2000/JPX, TIFF, CMYK JPEG) OR the code immediately uses only a subpart (e.g., getRaster/getData) without other BufferedImage-specific needs; and there is no preceding explicit ImageReader acquisition and no reader.setInput(ImageInputStream) in the same decoding path.

B) Unnecessary image conversion: a helper method $CONVERTER.$toRGBImageMethod($wr,$cs) (or similarly named) is used to build a new BufferedImage from a WritableRaster whose layout/data type matches $cs such that a direct new BufferedImage(new ComponentColorModel(...), $wr, false, null) would suffice; and the result is returned/used without further required color management.

C) Generic per-sample color conversion in a hot inner loop: nested loops over width/height (or a single loop over total samples) invoke ColorSpace.toRGB/ColorSpace.getInstance(...).toRGB, Math.pow per component, and/or matrix element getters per iteration; intermediate arrays are allocated inside the loop; results are written per sample to the output raster/buffer.

D) Redundant pre-copy before full overwrite: after obtaining raw/banded data via a low-level read (e.g., ImageReader.readRaster, getRawData), the code creates a compatible output and performs an immediate full copy (setRect/arraycopy/clone), followed by a traversal that overwrites most/all output elements regardless of the copied values.

E) Missing semantic fast-paths: a code branch explicitly labeled or implied as invisible/zero-opacity or handling different mask semantics performs drawing with an opaque Color/Composite, or applies a single alpha computation for multiple mask modes without a mode flag (e.g., no inversion for explicit masks).
negative_constraints: Do not match if an explicit ImageReader is obtained, an ImageInputStream is created, reader.setInput(...) is called, capabilities are checked (canReadRaster/canDecodeInput), and reader.read/readRaster is used appropriately for the format.
Do not match convenience ImageIO.read for simple, efficiently supported formats (e.g., baseline PNG/JPEG) when no special capabilities or partial reads are required.

Do not match if conversion is required for correctness (e.g., ICC transforms with nontrivial intents, gamma/transfer functions, different data types like short/float, premultiplied alpha constraints) and cannot be expressed by a direct ColorModel+Raster wrap.
Do not match if the hot-loop conversion already uses a precomputed LUT, cached matrix primitives, or a fast-path that avoids per-sample Math.pow/ColorSpace.toRGB calls and per-iteration allocations.
Do not match redundant-copy pattern if the initial copy is needed for later independent use (snapshot), or if only a small subset is updated subsequently.

Do not match invisible/semantics branch if the code sets alpha=0 via Color/AlphaComposite or skips drawing entirely, or already distinguishes mask modes via a boolean/enum flag with correct per-element math.
signals: Calls to ImageIO.read(InputStream|File|URL) near identifiers/strings: "JBIG2", "JPX", "JPEG2000", "TIFF", "CMYK", "YCCK", "RAW"
Absence of ImageReader.getImageReadersByFormatName/MIMEType and reader.setInput(ImageInputStream) on the same path
Immediate getRaster()/getData() after ImageIO.read(...)
Helper names like toRGBImageAWT, toRGBImage, convertToRGB(...) returning BufferedImage from WritableRaster
Presence of ColorSpace.getInstance(...).toRGB(...) or cs.toRGB(...) inside nested loops over pixels
Multiple Math.pow(...) and matrix.getValue(i,j) calls per pixel; new float[]{...} allocations in the loop
SequenceInputStream used to compose streams passed to ImageIO.read(...)
Low-level reads: ImageReader.readRaster(...), getDataBuffer(), followed by out.setRect(in) and then a full traversal overwriting out
Comments/identifiers: BGR->RGB, CMYK->RGB, channel reorder, fast-path
Branches named INVISIBLE/NEITHER_FILL_NOR_STROKE or code paths with opacity==0 using Color.BLACK/new Color(r,g,b) without alpha

type_and_flow_constraints: StreamLike represents an encoded binary stream with filter/encoding metadata; examples: PDF COSStream, image streams, compressed blobs
SRC: StreamLike with methods openDecodedInput()/createInputStream(), openRawInput()/createRawInputStream(), getEncodingMetadata()/getFilters()
DST: StreamLike with methods openEncodedOutput()/createOutputStream(), openRawOutput(meta)/createOutputStream(meta) that accept filters/encoding metadata
DECODER/ENCODER are codec APIs (e.g., ImageIO, filter decode/encode) that transcode content
Clone/merge path intent: DST content is derived solely from SRC content, with no semantic transformation required
Aliasing may occur (DST == SRC or share underlying storage); if so, writing must not start until reading is fully buffered/finished
Data-flow shows full materialization (byte[] or ByteArrayOutputStream) or direct decoded copy without any compatibility guard
matching_rules: Method or call chain belongs to a clone/merge/copy/import/append operation over encoded streams (identifier or callsite contains merge|clone|copy|append|import)

Detect one of: (A) decode-then-encode pair on the path (DECODER.decode + ENCODER.encode or ImageIO.read + ImageIO.write) without intervening transformation, or (B) IO.copy from SRC.openDecodedInput() to DST.openEncodedOutput() without passing SRC's encoding metadata, or (C) same receiver variable used for both create/open InputStream and OutputStream in the same scope
Presence of full buffering when transcoding or copying (use of byte[], ByteArrayOutputStream, IO.readAllBytes, IOUtils.toByteArray) in a clone path
Absence of a compatibility guard: no branch that checks DST.supports(SRC.getEncodingMetadata()) or equivalent before choosing a raw passthrough path
When an API offers metadata-aware output (createOutputStream(meta)/openRawOutput(meta)), the code uses the zero-arg variant while SRC.getEncodingMetadata()/getFilters() is in scope
negative_constraints: Exclude if the code performs necessary transformations (e.g., color space conversion, scaling, transparency changes, normalization, encryption policy change) that require decode and re-encode
Exclude if there is an explicit compatibility check and a raw passthrough path using raw input and metadata-propagating output when encodings match
Exclude if the copy uses raw-to-raw streaming passthrough without full materialization (e.g., IO.copy(SRC.openRawInput(), DST.openRawOutput(SRC.meta)))
Exclude if SRC and DST are guaranteed distinct and the OutputStream is created only after the InputStream has been fully consumed and closed (no read-while-write hazard)
Exclude when the target API lacks any notion of raw vs decoded I/O or encoding metadata, making passthrough impossible
Exclude unit tests or sample code that intentionally re-encodes for validation
signals: Calls to ImageIO.read(...)/ImageIO.write(...), or matching DECODER.decode(...) and ENCODER.encode(...) pairs in clone/copy paths
Use of IOUtils.copy(InputStream, OutputStream) where the InputStream is decoded and the OutputStream is encoded
Zero-arg createOutputStream()/openEncodedOutput() used while SRC.getFilters()/getEncoding()/getEncodingMetadata() is available but unused
Presence of API pairs like createInputStream vs createRawInputStream, createOutputStream vs createOutputStream(Filters) in the same scope
Full buffering via ByteArrayOutputStream, IOUtils.toByteArray, InputStream.readAllBytes in clone/copy routines
Filter/encoding names in scope: DCTDecode/JPEG, CCITTFaxDecode, FlateDecode, LZWDecode
Profiles showing CPU in Inflater/Deflater, ImageIO codecs during merge/clone operations
Same receiver variable used for both createInputStream and createOutputStream within a method
canonical_examples: void appendImage(StreamLike src, StreamLike dst) throws IOException { BufferedImage img = ImageIO.read(src.openDecodedInput()); try (OutputStream out = dst.openEncodedOutput()) { ImageIO.write(img, "jpg", out); } } // Fix: if (dst.supports(src.getEncodingMetadata())) { try (InputStream rin = src.openRawInput(); OutputStream rout = dst.openRawOutput(src.getEncodingMetadata())) { IOUtils.copy(rin, rout); } }

void copyCosStream(COSStream src, COSStream dst) throws IOException { try (InputStream in = src.createInputStream(); OutputStream out = dst.createOutputStream()) { IOUtils.copy(in, out); } } // Fix: try (InputStream in = src.createRawInputStream(); OutputStream out = dst.createOutputStream(src.getFilters())) { IOUtils.copy(in, out); }

root_cause: Thread-safety violations in lazy initialization and put-once cache logic (non-atomic check-then-act, missing re-checks, and missing slot/value guards).
type_and_flow_constraints: F is a shared field (instance or static) read before any lock is acquired and may be written inside a synchronized block; it is not final and not guaranteed to be volatile.
CACHE is a shared, non-concurrent container (array, HashMap, or custom map) storing V by key/index K; updates are not done via atomic map operations.
COUNT is a plain int (not AtomicInteger) used to track cache occupancy or a limit; COUNT++ is used near cache writes.
LOCK is a monitor object used with synchronized(LOCK) or synchronized method; may be distinct from this.
EXPENSIVE_COMPUTE uses CPU/IO heavy work and may access SharedResource S (e.g., seek/position/read/parse) with side effects on S.
Method getOrLoad is externally accessible (public/protected or called across threads) and can be concurrently invoked with identical K.
Assignment to F or CACHE_put writes V derived from EXPENSIVE_COMPUTE; in FIELD mode, F is assigned; in PER-KEY mode, CACHE[k] is assigned.
matching_rules: Match if any of the following holds:

A) Missing inner re-check in lazy init: there exists a method that executes if (F == null) { synchronized(LOCK) { INIT_OR_ASSIGN(F); } } where INIT_OR_ASSIGN may assign to F directly or via helper, and there is no F == null re-check inside the synchronized block before assigning/initializing.

B) Put-once violation under lock: inside synchronized(LOCK), code computes V v = EXPENSIVE_COMPUTE(...); then, if (CACHE != null && COUNT < MAX) { CACHE_put(CACHE, k, v); COUNT++; } without guarding both v != null and that the target slot/key in CACHE is currently empty (CACHE[k] == null or !containsKey(k)).

C) Unsynchronized memoization: a method reads and conditionally writes to CACHE (or increments COUNT) without holding any lock or using atomic/concurrent structures, following a pattern like if (CACHE != null && CACHE_get(...) != null) return ...; V v = EXPENSIVE_COMPUTE(...); if (CACHE != null && COUNT < MAX) { CACHE_put(...); COUNT++; }

D) Recompute-under-lock without memoization: a synchronized method or synchronized(LOCK) block performs EXPENSIVE_COMPUTE using a shared resource S for key k on every call and returns the result, while no field-based memoization (Map/array indexed by k or a shared F) is checked before locking; repeated calls with same k redo the work under contention.
For A/C/B, F/CACHE/COUNT must be class fields (not locals) and read/written along the described control flow.
negative_constraints: Exclude proper double-checked locking: if (F == null) { synchronized(LOCK) { if (F == null) F = compute(...); } } with F declared volatile or using correct publication.
Exclude accessors where the entire method is synchronized and the null check on F occurs while the lock is held (and initialization happens only once with an inner null guard).
Exclude caches implemented with ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent/putIfAbsent or equivalent atomic check-then-act.
Exclude cases where COUNT is derived from cache.size() or updated atomically (AtomicInteger/LongAdder) with slot emptiness checks.
Exclude logic that already checks both (v != null) and (slot empty: CACHE[k] == null or !containsKey(k)) before mutating CACHE and COUNT.
Exclude thread-confined or ThreadLocal caches/fields not observable across threads.
Exclude computations where per-call variation is required (e.g., depends on time/random/external side effects making caching incorrect).
signals: Pattern: if (field == null) synchronized(lock) { INIT(); } with no inner if (field == null) inside the synchronized block.
Synchronized block or method that assigns to a shared field or writes to a shared array/HashMap, followed by COUNT++.
Cache writes like CACHE[index] = v or CACHE.put(k, v) near COUNT++ and a check COUNT < MAX.
Absence of checks v != null and slot empty (CACHE[k] == null or !containsKey(k)) before put and COUNT++.
Use of non-concurrent structures (HashMap, arrays) for cross-thread memoization; missing volatile/Atomic/Lock usage for involved fields.
Helper called inside synchronized that assigns to the same shared field (F) or cache.
Shared IO resource with position/seek/save/restore calls inside synchronized; method named get*/read*/load*/init* with key/index parameter.
Field names: cache, glyphs, buffer, table, entries; counters named count/size/numCached; constants MAX_*/LIMIT.

type_and_flow_constraints: IN ∈ {InputStream, PushbackInputStream, types exposing pread via PositionedReadable/FSDataInputStream-like, or wrappers that also implement Seekable}
OUT ∈ {OutputStream, ByteArrayOutputStream, NullOutputStream-like}; MAYBE_UNREAD requires IN to support unread(byte[], int, int) if used
KEY is a byte[] sentinel (length m ≥ 2) when sentinel scanning is present; K is a small fixed constant (e.g., 4 or 8) when assembling a primitive
ACC is an accumulator/state: for fixed-size primitives, integer/long bit accumulator; for scanning, a small DFA state such as matched prefix length
In the positional variant, the position argument equals BASE + DONE where DONE is monotonically increasing by bytes read; access pattern is sequential over a contiguous region
REUSABLE_BUF is a non-trivial byte[] (length > 1) reused across loop iterations; readFully handles partial reads
If LIMIT is specified, the buffered loop must not read past LIMIT in semantic terms (ensure the consumer respects the bound or truncates processing)
If SEEK is used, IN must support Seekable.getPos/seek; after the fix, sequential reads use read(byte[], off, len) without per-iteration positional arguments
No cross-thread sharing of IN that would require positional reads to preserve per-thread cursor semantics
matching_rules: Find a loop (for/while/do) where the body issues per-iteration I/O of exactly one byte via InputStream.read() without an intermediate byte[] buffer; optional EOFException or break on -1

OR: Find a loop where the body invokes a positional read API (e.g., read(long pos, byte[], int, int), pread, positionedRead) each iteration with pos == BASE + ACCUMULATED_BYTES, and ACCUMULATED_BYTES increases monotonically
Per-byte path indicators: (b & 0xFF) << (8*k) patterns OR nested if-chains comparing successive bytes against ASCII/keyword constants; frequent OutputStream.write(int)
PushbackInputStream.unread(...) or unread(byte[], ...) may appear upon detecting a delimiter
Absence of a reusable bulk buffer feeding the loop: either no byte[] buffer is present, or a 1-byte buffer is used, or the buffer is refilled through single-byte reads

After the fix, bulk read(byte[], off, len) replaces either read() single-byte calls or positional reads; optional initial seek aligns stream position; scanning happens over the filled buffer with carry-over of partial matches
negative_constraints: Exclude when the method already performs bulk reads into a byte[] and scans within that buffer (no per-byte read or per-iteration positional read)
Exclude genuine random-access patterns where positions are non-monotonic or revisit earlier offsets
Exclude concurrency-driven designs where positional reads are required to avoid altering shared stream state across threads
Exclude sources that only expose positional reads (no seek) and where switching to seek+read is impossible

Exclude variable-length encodings (e.g., varints) where loop termination depends on continuation bits and the code intentionally reads one byte at a time with small, bounded length not amenable to readFully replacement
Exclude cases where the data source is an in-memory byte[] or ByteBuffer accessed by indexing without I/O calls
Exclude if OutputStream writes are already batched (write(byte[], off, len)) and there is no per-byte write within the loop
signals: Tight loops with InputStream.read() returning int used as a byte, often followed by (x & 0xFF) and << shift by multiples of 8
Deeply nested byte comparisons against ASCII constants for delimiter/keyword detection
Frequent OutputStream.write(int) calls inside the loop
EOFException or similar thrown directly on read() < 0 in the loop
Repeated calls to read(position, buf, off, len)/pread with pos == base + accumulatedBytes
Presence of PushbackInputStream.unread(...) to push back a matched sentinel
Performance counters or logs indicating many small reads or excessive block read operations
canonical_examples:
Before: int readInt(InputStream in) throws IOException { int n = 0; for (int i=0, s=0; i<4; i++, s+=8) { int b = in.read(); if (b < 0) throw new EOFException(); n |= ((b & 0xFF) << s); } return n; }
After: int readInt(InputStream in) throws IOException { byte[] buf = TMP4; readFully(in, buf, 0, 4); return ((buf[0] & 0xFF)) | ((buf[1] & 0xFF) << 8) | ((buf[2] & 0xFF) << 16) | ((buf[3] & 0xFF) << 24); }

Before: while (copied < len) { int n = src.pread(offset + copied, tmp, 0, tmp.length); if (n <= 0) break; dst.write(tmp, 0, n); copied += n; }
After: if (src.getPos() != offset) src.seek(offset); for (int n; copied < len && (n = src.read(buf, 0, Math.min(buf.length, (int)(len - copied)))) > 0; ) { dst.write(buf, 0, n); copied += n; }

root_cause: Redundant computation due to eager diagnostic message construction on the fast path
type_and_flow_constraints: LOGGER is a logging facade/impl supporting level guards and/or parameterized messages (e.g., SLF4J, Log4j, JUL via adapter). LEVEL ∈ {TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR} (or analogous).

EXPENSIVE_EXPR_i includes any of: OBJ.toString() where OBJ is non-trivial; Arrays.toString/Arrays.asList; String.format; new StringBuilder + .append chains; iteration over a collection to assemble details; method calls performing I/O/computation; object/array allocations for varargs.
For Case A, no dominating guard if (LOGGER.is<LEVEL>Enabled()) encloses the computation of msg/ARG_i; the heavy construction occurs on the normal (non-error) path.

For Case B, method is com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkState|checkArgument|checkNotNull with signature (boolean, String, Object...) or equivalent; COND does not depend on EXPENSIVE_EXPR_i; the EXPENSIVE_EXPR_i are not used elsewhere.
The precomputed msg/values are only consumed by the diagnostic sink (logging or exception/precondition message) and have no required side effects.
Hot path context: the site is inside a loop or a frequently invoked method/handler, or executed per item/event/request.
matching_rules: Match a MethodInvocation to a logging method: LOGGER.debug/info/trace/warn/error(...), LOG.log(LEVEL, ...), etc.

Within the logging call or immediately before it, detect any of: (a) binary string concatenation '+' with non-literals; (b) ClassInstanceCreation of StringBuilder/StringBuffer with subsequent appends; (c) String.format(...) used to compute a String; (d) presence of .toString(), String.valueOf(...), Arrays.toString(...), Arrays.asList(...), collection iteration whose result feeds the message.
Verify that the logging call and any message construction are not enclosed by a guard is<LEVEL>Enabled()/isEnabled(LEVEL) that dominates the expensive construction.

Match a MethodInvocation to Preconditions.checkState|checkArgument|checkNotNull with a format string plus ≥1 vararg where at least one vararg is a non-trivial expression (method call, allocation, concatenation, toString/Arrays.*).
For Preconditions, ensure the call is not inside a failure-only branch (no surrounding if (!COND) ... that would evaluate message only on failure).
Ensure the expensive intermediate (if any, e.g., msg variable) is single-use for diagnostics and not consumed by functional logic.
Optionally, favor sites at INFO/DEBUG/TRACE levels and within loops or per-event handlers to prioritize hot paths.
negative_constraints: Exclude logging calls already enclosed by an appropriate guard (if (LOGGER.is<LEVEL>Enabled()) { ... }) that wraps the expensive construction, or frameworks using a lazy Supplier/lambda for the message.

Exclude parameterized logging that passes objects directly without precomputing strings (e.g., LOGGER.debug("msg {}", obj)) unless additional eager construction (toString/valueOf/concatenation) is present.
Exclude cases where the computed string/data is also used for non-diagnostic control flow or has required side effects.
Exclude WARN/ERROR/FATAL logs reporting actual errors where message construction cost is acceptable/intentional or mandated by requirements.
Exclude precondition/assert calls that use only constant messages or trivial variable references (no expensive varargs), or APIs that accept a lazy Supplier<String> evaluated only on failure.
Exclude startup/shutdown/admin-only code paths that are executed rarely (cold path), when identifiable.
signals: Presence of "+" string concatenation or new StringBuilder(...) immediately feeding LOGGER.*(...).
Use of .toString(), String.valueOf(...), Arrays.toString(...), Arrays.asList(...) inside LOGGER.*(...) arguments.
Local variable named msg/sb/repr built before a log/throw and not used elsewhere.
LOGGER.info/debug/trace(...) without a preceding isInfoEnabled/isDebugEnabled/isTraceEnabled guard.
Preconditions.checkState|checkArgument with a format and multiple args where args include method calls, Arrays.* conversions, or toString().
Commits that change .info(...) to .debug/.trace and add isXEnabled() guards, or rewrite Preconditions.checkX(...) into if (!COND) throw ... with deferred formatting.

root_cause: Inefficient algorithms/data structures due to missing or too-low expansion bounds (configuration-related), leading to algorithmic blowups or slow fallback paths
generalized_template: R out = EXPAND_OP(CI, A1, ..., Ak [, L_SMALL]);  // L_SMALL omitted or equals a small/default cap controlling expansion/determinization
type_and_flow_constraints: EXPAND_OP ∈ {constructor or method performing size-expanding transformation}: e.g., new CompiledAutomaton(...), Operations.determinize(...), Operations.minimize(...), RegExp.toAutomaton(...), Automata.makeStringUnion(...), Graph/Trie builders
CI (Complex Input) ∈ {Automaton, RegExp/Pattern, Collection<String>/TermSet, Query-like structures, Graph/Trie source}; may be large or highly complex
There exists an overload or configuration for EXPAND_OP that accepts a numeric cap parameter L: int|long with semantics {maxStates, maxDeterminizedStates, capacity, limit, threshold}
If L is present, its value is a constant/literal or DEFAULT_* style field representing a conservative/small cap; if L is absent, the chosen overload uses an internal default cap
The result out is consumed by code expecting or benefiting from full/efficient expansion/determinization (e.g., CompiledAutomaton/CompiledStructure, downstream assertions/properties)
No subsequent reconfiguration raises the cap before out is used (no later setMax*/reconstruction with higher L)
matching_rules: Match a ConstructorInvocation or MethodInvocation EXPAND_OP where either (a) the cap argument L is missing while an overload with L exists, or (b) L is provided but bound to a small/default constant (identifier matches DEFAULT_MAX_*, *_LIMIT, *_CAP, *_THRESHOLD or similar)
Confirm via symbol resolution that an alternative overload exists with an additional int/long cap parameter affecting expansion complexity
CI originates from complex sources: new RegExp(...).toAutomaton(), makeStringUnion(...), wildcard/regex pattern compilation, union of many terms, or an Automaton/graph produced upstream
If inside a wrapper API (e.g., Query/Parser/Builder constructor), check that the wrapper does not accept or propagate a max/cap parameter to EXPAND_OP
Optional strengthening: immediate uses assert or rely on determinization/minimization completeness (e.g., isDeterministic(), language-equivalence checks, creating CompiledAutomaton)
negative_constraints: Exclude if an explicit high/unbounded cap is already passed (e.g., Integer.MAX_VALUE or a large configured value) or the efficient algorithmic path is guaranteed
Exclude calls where the extra argument is unrelated to performance (e.g., debug flags, comparators, enum modes not controlling expansion size)
Exclude if prior checks provably bound CI size/complexity so the default cap is sufficient (validated by guards or preconditions)
Exclude if the transformation is lazy/streaming and does not materialize the expanded structure
Exclude code that intentionally enforces the cap and handles TooManyStates/TooComplex exceptions as part of normal control flow
Exclude if the limit value is user-configured for safety in production and documented as intentionally restrictive
signals: Overloads that differ only by an extra int/long parameter named maxDeterminizedStates, maxStates, maxNodes, capacity, limit, threshold
Use of constants named DEFAULT_MAX_*, *_LIMIT, *_CAP passed to expansion methods; fix replaces with Integer.MAX_VALUE or a much larger value
Calls like new CompiledAutomaton(automaton) or Operations.determinize(a) without a cap argument; fix switches to overload with cap
Inputs built from regex/wildcard patterns or large unions (e.g., RegExp.toAutomaton, Automata.makeStringUnion)
Performance symptoms reported near the callsite: exponential state growth, OOM/TooComplex/TooManyStates exceptions, long GC pauses
API changes in fixes that add and thread a max*/limit parameter through constructors and builders

root_cause: Inefficient data structures, Inefficiencies in third-party libraries or dependencies
type_and_flow_constraints: Num ∈ {int, long} or their boxed counterparts when stored in collections; Comparator, if present, must be equivalent to natural numeric ordering
C is a Collection<Num> or a Map view: M.keySet() with K ∈ Num, or M.values() with V ∈ Num
Population loop dominates all insertions that are considered by the subsequent Collections.max call; no intervening mutations that add/remove elements between the loop end and max computation
OFFSET is a compile-time constant or loop-invariant integer
USE_AS_SIZE_OR_INDEX(bound) includes array/buffer allocation, array indexing bounds, or pre-sizing of data structures
For Pattern B: IntLike ∈ {byte, short, char, int, long}; RHS POW2 is a compile-time constant equal to 2^K (K ≥ 1); mask width matches the LHS type width (for long, use long literals and masks)
For Pattern B: The intended semantics are unsigned wrap into [0..POW2-1]; EXPR does not rely on Java's signed remainder for distinguishing negative results
matching_rules:
Pattern A match:
    - Find a loop that executes ADD/PUT into a target collection/map C_src (or M) derived from the same method scope
    - After the loop, detect Collections.max(T, optComparator) where T is either the same collection C_src, M.keySet(), or M.values()
    - The result of Collections.max(...) (optionally plus/minus a small constant OFFSET) is used immediately as an allocation size, capacity hint, or index bound
    - The numeric quantity used for max can be computed at insertion time (the inserted key/value or a numeric derived from the loop element)

Pattern B match:
    - Detect an integer remainder operator '%' or '%=' where the divisor is a literal or compile-time constant that equals 2^K (e.g., 256, 65536, 0x100, 1<<K)
    - The expression occurs in a loop or method identified as hot (heuristic: in a tight loop, decoding/parsing, or followed by immediate indexing/keying)
    - The result is used to normalize/wrap a value into a fixed-width unsigned range (e.g., array index, glyph/code unit, hash bucket, byte/char/short normalization)
    - Types of EXPR and result are primitive int or long (or narrower promoted to int)
negative_constraints: Pattern A: Exclude if the collection/map is mutated (adds/removes) between the population loop and the Collections.max call by code not dominated by that loop
Pattern A: Exclude if a custom Comparator imposes a non-numeric or non-natural order (e.g., reverse with side conditions, non-total order) that cannot be reproduced by a simple max accumulator
Pattern A: Exclude if Collections.max is intentionally recomputed multiple times interleaved with mutations, making a single tracked max unsafe
Pattern B: Exclude if divisor is not an exact power of two or is not a compile-time constant
Pattern B: Exclude if code relies on signed remainder semantics for negatives (e.g., distinguishing -1 % 256 from 255 wrap)
Pattern B: Exclude BigInteger/BigDecimal or other non-primitive integer arithmetic
Pattern B: Exclude cases where masking would change width semantics (e.g., expecting >31-bit modulo in int, or long without 64-bit mask/literals)
signals: Collections.max(...) immediately after constructing/populating a Collection or Map
Collections.max over Map.keySet() or Map.values() used to size arrays or buffers (e.g., new byte[max+1])
Presence of boxing: Collection<Integer>/Collection<Long> populated then scanned by Collections.max
A preceding loop that inserted exactly the elements later scanned by Collections.max
Modulo by familiar power-of-two constants: % 256, % 65536, % 0x100, % 0x10000, % (1<<K)
Nearby constants of the form (1<<K)-1, 0xFF, 0xFFFF; usage as array index or mask operations
Hot/inner loops in parsing/decoding or raster/font processing routines

root_cause: Redundant repeated evaluation of expensive color functions/conversions in rasterization loops
type_and_flow_constraints: CS: pure, deterministic color-space-like converter (e.g., ColorSpace/ICC-based) exposing toRGB(float[]) or equivalent; no side effects between calls
F: pure, deterministic function mapping a single scalar float/double t to a small float[] (≤4 channels); its result depends only on t and immutable parameters
param(x,y): expression of loop indices only; its value is bounded within [T0, T1] for all iterations of the loops
T0 < T1 are finite bounds known or computable before the loops; N is a finite resolution independent of loop iteration count
LUT index depends only on t; LUT has fixed size N+1 and is initialized before any use
packRGB/unpack operations are side-effect-free and do not allocate per-iteration
fallbackVals (if used) are invariant for the lifetime of the rasterization and their conversion is safe to compute once
If a ThirdPartyContainer lookup is memoized, the container and key are immutable after construction; the returned value is constant and safely cacheable for the CLASS instance
Thread-safety: cached fields are either confined to a thread or safely published (e.g., final, volatile, or proper synchronization) if instances are shared
matching_rules: Detect one or more loops (often nested) iterating over an image/grid domain and writing per-element color data into an array/buffer (e.g., byte[]/int[]/WritableRaster)
Inside the innermost loop, identify an expensive call chain of the form vals = F.eval/apply(t); rgb = CS.toRGB(vals) (or similar color conversion) executed per iteration
The scalar parameter t is computed from loop indices (x,y, or i,j) and is independent of other mutable state; its domain can be bounded to [T0, T1]
The result of CS.toRGB(...) is immediately packed or copied into output channels; frequent per-iteration float[] temporaries or Math.min/Math.max clamps around channels are present
A constant or fallback color conversion (e.g., background/overprint) is recomputed inside the loop and reused in multiple iterations
Optionally, getters used by F/CS repeatedly call immutable third-party container lookups (dict.get*(CONST_KEY)) on every invocation
negative_constraints: Exclude if F or CS.toRGB have side effects or depend on mutable state varying per iteration beyond the scalar parameter (e.g., global mutable caches, I/O, randomness)
Exclude if t cannot be reasonably bounded or discretized to a 1D LUT without violating correctness/quality requirements (visible banding or unacceptable quantization error)
Exclude if the function depends on multiple independent variables (true 2D/3D domain) making LUT dimensionality or memory impractical
Exclude if per-iteration calls are already cheap (simple arithmetic or field access) and LUT/memoization would not measurably reduce cost
Exclude if the container lookup/memoized value can change after construction or must reflect mutations (would lead to stale reads)
Exclude contexts requiring strict NaN-propagation semantics if clamping/packs alter behavior in ways that affect correctness
signals: Nested loops writing to pixel buffers with patterns like out[idx++] = ..., or (r<<16)|(g<<8)|b packing
Per-iteration calls to methods named toRGB, toRGBImage, ColorSpace.toRGB, or Function.eval/evaluate
Per-iteration allocations of float[] channel arrays or temporary buffers
Repeated computation of the same background/fallback color conversion inside the loop
Introduction or presence of int[]/byte[] lookup tables named lut/lookup/cache in fixes
Discretization index computed via cast and clamp: (int)((t - T0) * N / (T1 - T0)) with Math.min/Math.max
Third-party containers (e.g., COSDictionary or ICC profiles) accessed via get*(CONST_KEY) inside getters used in hot paths

type_and_flow_constraints: SOURCE is long-lived or reused across many queries; its cardinality is not trivially small.

PRED depends only on stable, derivable attributes from e and q: (a) equality or canonical key; (b) numeric coordinates with a tolerance forming axis-aligned ranges; or (c) interval membership Range<T>.contains(point).
For EQUALITY: KEY_OF_E and KEY_OF(q) are deterministic and keys are unique within SOURCE (or uniqueness is enforced during index build).
For ORDERED_RANGE: X, Y, and D are numeric and Comparable; tolerance D is derived from q and is loop-invariant for the candidate scan; no ordering semantics of the original List are required.
For INTERVAL: T is Comparable; ranges are closed or have well-defined contains semantics; query is point-based.
Indexes are built once per context or maintained incrementally on updates; concurrent access must respect visibility (e.g., final fields, safe publication, or concurrent maps).
Early-return scans (e.g., return index or first match) are semantically equivalent to indexed lookup results.
If results are accumulated into a collection (e.g., Set<V>), the index lookup returns an equivalent collection without requiring a full scan.
matching_rules: Detect a hot method that, per invocation, iterates a collection or map entries and selects elements via a predicate PRED(e, q) where q is the method parameter or derived from it.

Equality/type resolution variant: a loop over a fixed List/Collection returning the loop index or element when MATCHES(alt, q) holds (e.g., instanceOf, name/schema matching), otherwise throws/returns empty.

Numeric proximity variant: Map<K, List<E>> or similar bucketing; for each incoming item, linearly scan the List<E> using Math.abs(a - b) <= tol (possibly for 2D) to set a found/suppress flag, then add when not found.
Interval membership variant: iterate Map<Range<T>, Collection<V>> or Multimap<Range<T>, V>; inside the loop call range.contains(point) and accumulate matches into a new collection per call.
The method is executed frequently (e.g., called in tight loops, hot paths, or request processing) while the underlying data grows or is non-trivial in size.

The optimized version introduces or uses an index field (Map, NavigableMap/NavigableSet, or IntervalIndex) built at construction/rebuild time or maintained via add/remove, and replaces the scan with a direct lookup (get/subMap/subSet/query).
negative_constraints: Exclude if SOURCE is frequently mutated in ways not reflected in the index (stale index risk) and no maintenance path is present.
Exclude if PRED depends on transient or value-dependent state beyond stable keys/ranges (e.g., requires visiting all elements for side effects).
Exclude if key uniqueness cannot be guaranteed or ambiguity is semantically meaningful (cannot map to a single entry).
Exclude if List iteration order is semantically required for correctness and the indexed structure would change behavior.
Exclude if metrics are non-orderable or require non-axis-aligned proximity (e.g., arbitrary distance without an order decomposition), making range trees inapplicable.
Exclude when per-call data size is provably tiny and queries are infrequent (no measurable benefit).
Exclude if an indexed or logarithmic lookup is already in place (e.g., NavigableMap/TreeSet.subMap/subSet, interval tree).
signals: For-loops over collections with immediate return of loop index or element upon predicate match; throws if not found.
Map<..., List<...>> used as an index; inner loop with Math.abs(...) <= tol and a suppress/found boolean flag.
Iteration over Map.Entry<Range<...>, Collection<...>> with entry.getKey().contains(point) and allocation of a new HashSet/ArrayList on each query.
Introduction of fields like Map<K, Integer>/Map<K, A> built in a constructor/init, or NavigableMap/NavigableSet for numeric dimensions, or a custom IntervalIndex/RangeIndex class.
Calls to subMap(...), subSet(...), ceiling/floor, or query(point) replacing linear scans.
Helper methods added to compute canonical keys (e.g., full type/schema name) or to extract numeric coordinates/tolerance.

set.contains(element.getAnnotationType()) or similar set.contains(element.getX()) called on each element inside a for-each filter loop where getX() (e.g., getAnnotationType(), getParameterTypes()) could be expensive; result is per-element but getX() itself is not cached in a local variable before the contains call

root_cause: Improper I/O usage, Inefficient or bad API usage
type_and_flow_constraints: CS has static type CharSequence (or subtype) and originates from in-memory data (e.g., String, GString, StringBuilder/StringBuffer, CharSequence-returning API), not from external I/O

READ_ALL_LINES is a call that fully materializes lines into a List<String>/Collection<String> from a Reader or String (e.g., IOGroovyMethods.readLines(Reader), IOUtils.readLines(Reader), Files.readAllLines(Path), custom readAllLines(Reader))
The materialized list L is consumed in a single linear pass (single for-each or equivalent) and is not relied upon for random access, mutation, or multiple traversals
Optional checked IOException is declared or caught due to using Reader-based APIs, even though only in-memory data is processed

For Pattern B, all uses of S after S = CS.toString() are limited to operations that are equally available on CharSequence (length, charAt, subSequence/substring, simple concatenation, or passing to APIs that accept CharSequence)

If snapshot semantics are required (CS may be mutable and content could change across uses), only match when code does not rely on capturing a stable String snapshot (or when conversion can be deferred to the final boundary)
matching_rules: Find an expression E_CS with static type CharSequence used to construct a Reader via new StringReader(E_CS.toString()) (or equivalent CharSequence->String->Reader wrapping)
From that Reader (or from E_CS.toString()), detect a call that eagerly reads all lines into a List/Collection of Strings
Verify the resulting List is iterated once (enhanced for, index-based single pass, or stream-forEach derived from the list) and not used for random access, sorting, or multiple passes
Optionally, detect that the method declares throws IOException or has a try/catch(IOException) solely because of the Reader-based call on in-memory data

Alternatively (Pattern B), detect a local assignment String S = E_CS.toString(); where subsequent uses of S are restricted to CharSequence-level operations and/or passing to methods that also accept CharSequence

Confirm there exists an alternative API to iterate lazily or accept CharSequence directly (e.g., line iterator over CharSequence or overloads that take CharSequence) or that CharSequence operations can replace String-only conveniences used
negative_constraints: Exclude when the source is actual external I/O (e.g., FileReader, Socket, URLConnection, Files.newBufferedReader) rather than an in-memory CharSequence

Exclude when the materialized list L is intentionally needed for random access, multiple traversals, size-dependent decisions prior to iteration, or bulk operations requiring all lines resident (e.g., sorting all lines before processing)
Exclude when downstream APIs strictly require a Reader or a String and no CharSequence-based or lazy alternative exists
Exclude when String-specific semantics are intentionally relied upon (e.g., String.intern(), getBytes(Charset), regionMatches with locale-specific behavior) without a CharSequence-equivalent path
Exclude when immediate toString() is required to capture a stable snapshot because CS may mutate between uses and correctness depends on freezing the content
Exclude if the existing API already returns a lazy view (e.g., a line Stream that is not collected) and the code is not eagerly materializing
signals: new StringReader(<charseq>.toString())
Calls like readLines(Reader), IOUtils.readLines(...), IOGroovyMethods.readLines(...), Files.readAllLines(...) followed by immediate single-pass iteration
Local variable named lines or similar assigned from a read-all-lines API, then used only in one for-each loop
Method or block declares/catches IOException even though only in-memory text is processed
CharSequence.toString() used solely to satisfy an API that also has a CharSequence overload or to perform operations available on CharSequence
Large intermediate List<String> allocation visible in profiles or memory, with simple per-line processing
canonical_examples: List<String> lines = IOGroovyMethods.readLines(new StringReader(cs.toString())); for (String line : lines) { handle(line); }
String s = cs.toString(); if (s.length() == 0) return s; return Character.toUpperCase(s.charAt(0)) + s.substring(1);

root_cause: Improper I/O usage: incorrect buffering strategy (redundant wrapping or missing buffering) that degrades performance or correctness
type_and_flow_constraints: S ∈ {InputStream, OutputStream, Reader, Writer}; BufferedX ∈ {BufferedInputStream, BufferedOutputStream, BufferedReader, BufferedWriter} with matching kind
S_base is file-backed or Files.* stream (or a method parameter of type S) and is unbuffered unless PARAM_S is already buffered

ONE_SHOT_IO(s, d) means exactly one write/read call with a fully materialized buffer or string (e.g., write(byte[]), write(String), read(byte[]) once), followed only by optional flush() and close() in the same scope
MULTI_STEP_IO(s) means multiple small reads/writes (e.g., inside a loop), or passing s to a routine that performs sequential/streaming I/O (e.g., save/copy/process/parse) with multiple operations
No semantic-transforming wrappers (e.g., GZIPOutputStream, CipherOutputStream, PrintWriter formatting, OutputStreamWriter charset bridging) are inserted or required solely by the buffering layer
Aliasing: S_buf or S_unbuf are not reused across long-lived contexts; their lifetime is confined to the observed method/scope unless PARAM_S is an input parameter
If PARAM_S is already an instance of BufferedX, wrapping it again constitutes redundant buffering
matching_rules:
Over-buffered (redundant) match if any of the following hold:
  - new BufferedX(Files.newOutputStream(...|Files.newInputStream(...))) (or File{Input|Output}Stream) is created and used for ONE_SHOT_IO followed by close/flush in the same scope,
  - new BufferedX(s) where s is already an instance of BufferedX (nested buffering),
  - new BufferedX(s) occurs unconditionally on a parameter s without any guard like (s instanceof BufferedX) and the subsequent usage does not require buffering (e.g., single bulk op).

Under-buffered (missing) match if:
  - new FileInputStream(...) or new FileOutputStream(...[, append]) or Files.newInputStream/OutputStream(...) is created and used directly without any BufferedX (or equivalent buffered) wrapper, and
  - MULTI_STEP_IO is detected: repeated small read()/write() calls (e.g., inside loops) or the stream is passed to an API that performs sequential processing (e.g., save/copy/process/load/serialize) performing multiple I/O operations.
negative_constraints: Exclude if multiple small writes/reads are performed and a proper BufferedX wrapper is already present (buffering is appropriate)

Exclude if the wrapper adds required semantics beyond buffering (e.g., GZIP/Cipher streams, PrintWriter formatting, OutputStreamWriter/OutputStreamReader for charset conversion); in such cases, only flag redundant extra BufferedX on top of a buffered chain, not the semantic wrapper itself
Exclude one-shot trivial small I/O (e.g., writing a short constant string or reading a known small header) where buffering is unnecessary and cost is negligible
Exclude when using NIO channels, Files.newBuffered* helpers, or memory-mapped I/O providing equivalent buffering
Exclude sockets/network streams where buffering strategy is dictated by protocol or latency constraints and cannot be inferred locally
signals: new BufferedOutputStream(Files.newOutputStream(...
new BufferedWriter(new OutputStreamWriter(Files.newOutputStream(...
new BufferedWriter(new FileWriter(... or new BufferedOutputStream(new FileOutputStream(... with only one write(...) before close
Exactly one occurrence of write(byte[]|String)/read(byte[]) on the wrapped object followed by flush() and close() in the same scope
Unconditional new BufferedReader/BufferedInputStream/BufferedWriter/BufferedOutputStream on a parameter without instanceof BufferedX guard
Nested buffering: new BufferedX(new BufferedX(...))
Direct new FileInputStream(...) or new FileOutputStream(...) passed to methods named save/write/copy/process/load/parse without a BufferedX wrapper
Loops with small buffer sizes performing read()/write() on unbuffered file streams
